references.text: Earlier in the chapter, God gives instructions to choose a lamb for each household and slaughter it - Moses now conveys these instructions to Israel's elders.
Moses was asked to gather Israel's elders, which he now does to give them Passover instructions.
Israel's elders are mentioned as representatives of the people, just as they are here when Moses speaks to them.
Repetition of the Passover command with instructions on how to slaughter the Passover lamb.
King Hezekiah celebrates Passover and the people slaughter the Passover lambs, in accordance with Moses' original instructions.
King Josiah celebrates Passover and gives instructions to slaughter the Passover lamb according to Moses' law.
After the exile, the priests and Levites slaughter the Passover lambs for the returning Israelites.
The book of Hebrews refers to how Moses instituted Passover and the sprinkling of blood by faith.
Paul calls Christ our Passover lamb who has been sacrificed, linking it to the original Passover slaughter.
John the Baptist calls Jesus 'the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world,' a reference to the Passover lamb.
Fulfillment that no bone shall be broken on the Passover lamb, applied to Jesus at the crucifixion.
Peter describes Christ as a spotless lamb and links salvation to the symbolism of the Passover lamb.
Highlights the continuity in Passover observance from the Exodus to the Sinai years.
Shows how Josiah's Passover celebration was a direct fulfillment of Moses' original command.
Direct narrative connection: Preparation (v.21) and the start of the Exodus (v.31).
Refers to the same type of event (meeting with an elder) in the Exodus narrative.
